edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber II 1

source_text: Nigra sum et formosa, filiae Hierusalem, sicut tabernacula Cedar, sicut pellae Salomonis. Incipit Liber Secundus. Sponsa ad filias Hierusalem loquitur, id est ad animas quae adhuc ex parte carnales sunt. Nigra propter paenitentiam, propter certamina, propter corpus humilitatis; formosa propter imaginem Dei, propter conversionem, propter sponsum qui eam dilexit. Cedar obscuritatem, pellae Salomonis decorem significant.
pass_a_gloss: Black I-am and beautiful, daughters of-Jerusalem, as tents of-Kedar, as curtains of-Solomon. Begins Book Second. Bride unto daughters of-Jerusalem speaks...
pass_b_english: [[I am black and beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:5]]. The Second Book begins. The Bride speaks to the daughters of Jerusalem — souls still partly carnal. She is black because of penitence, struggles, and the body of humility; beautiful because of the image of God, conversion, and the Bridegroom who loved her. Kedar signifies darkness; Solomon’s curtains, adornment.
